title: Build Evals That Actually Matter - Nick Ung & Akshay Sharma, Lyft
talk_summary: Lyft's customer-support agent team describes an end-to-end eval pipeline: offline multi-turn simulation with a fine-tuned user LLM and personas, binary task-success LLM judges validated as classifiers with precision/recall, and a continuous error-analysis loop feeding harness/context improvements. They stress that generic prebuilt metrics and un-gated judges are useless, and that eval criteria must co-evolve with observed data.

takeaways.technique: Binary task-success judges validated as classifiers
takeaways.what_they_do: Replace generic scores (helpfulness, naturalness) with a single pass/fail rubric tied to a business outcome, then hand-label ~100 examples and compute precision/recall against human ground truth to prove the judge works.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can hand label around 100 examples with pass fail labels ... then we score precision and recall for our judge based on human label ground truths

takeaways.technique: Gate on eval scores, not floating metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Only keep eval metrics that actually change a shipping decision; a judge score nobody gates on is worthless.

takeaways.technique: Config-driven eval harness run at multiple gates
takeaways.what_they_do: Define evals once in YAML (task, dataset, persona, model adapter, evaluator) and run the same suite locally, on prompt changes, at pre-commit, and in CI/CD with parallelism.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can define the config once and run these eval indefinitely many times across different ... gates of your agent development process
takeaways.numbers: thousands to tens of thousands of examples; needs parallelism/throughput

takeaways.technique: Realistic user simulator via fine-tune + personas
takeaways.what_they_do: Frontier models role-play users too politely, inflating pass rates; they fine-tune a user LLM on real verbatims and add personas (bypasser, refund-seeker, skeptic) so evals are realistically hard.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our first attempt ... gave us 90 plus pass rate ... this almost sounds too good to be true ... we fine-tune a LLM model with Lyft user verbatim

takeaways.technique: Continuous error-analysis loop on raw traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Regularly (weekly/biweekly) dive into logged traces, pinpoint failure modes, keep only decision-changing metrics, and feed findings into prompt/context/harness changes; not a one-off audit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this loop is something which runs continuously. It's not ... a one-off audit

takeaways.technique: Statistical rigor only where it matters
takeaways.what_they_do: Report confidence intervals and use paired designs; reserve expensive rigor for shipping decisions and leader reports, since small gains on 50 samples are noise.
